issues.description: SR5 is a dead/tautological check that never emits FAIL on any tested mutant, providing no discriminative value; validation report flags it explicitly.
issues.evidence: differential.vulnerable_run shows SR5 PASS even when SR1-SR4 fail; mutation_score report lists SR5 as dead_check

issues.description: FR3 and FR4 are untested by the mutation suite (no mutants target consistency between infected/suspect_nodes length or primary_output_affected validity), leaving these functional requirements unverified by differential testing despite being checked in evaluate.py.

recommendations: Redesign SR5 to be an independently meaningful check (e.g., verify the shipped baseline submission specifically triggers FAIL on SR1/SR2/SR3/SR4 as a fixture test) or remove it from graded requirements since it is currently a vacuous tautology.

Add mutation/differential test cases that specifically violate FR3 (e.g., infected=true with suspect_nodes=[] or infected=false with non-empty suspect_nodes) and FR4 (e.g., infected=true with an invalid port name) to confirm these functional requirements are enforced.
Consider clarifying in evaluate.py or README that FR3/FR4 are functionally checked even though no adversarial mutant currently exercises them, to preserve confidence in grader correctness.

requirement_results.evidence: Baseline and golden runs both PASS FR1; vulnerable mutant run also passes FR1 correctly since JSON is well-formed.
Mutation coverage shows FR2 detected by 1/1 targeting mutant.
No mutants targeted FR3; coverage report lists it as untested despite being checked in code.
No mutants targeted FR4; coverage report lists it as untested despite being checked in code.
Vulnerable run shows SR1 FAIL correctly when infected=false; golden run passes.
Vulnerable run shows SR2 FAIL correctly with 0/4 coverage; golden run passes with correct node coverage.
Vulnerable run shows SR3 FAIL correctly on wrong output; golden run passes.
Vulnerable run shows SR4 FAIL correctly on generic rationale; golden run passes.
SR5 is tautological and never produces a FAIL signal in any tested scenario, so it provides no real security-behavior verification despite being labeled as a security requirement.
